messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high-rate GPU driver resets detected on cluster 'infer-prod-eu' (metric: driver.reset.xid, rate: 18/min)
ops_oncall: ack, paging now. grabbing telemetry.
jen: seeing rising OOM + Xid 31 on hosts infer-eu-n[12-15]. nodes flapping, some containers restarting repeatedly.
liam: any customer impact yet?
samir: small percentage of requests are 5xx from the EU region, hitting heavy text-generation routes. sending bridge in a sec.
cs-bridge: bridging for affected tenants: alpha-game, docsai-pro. keeping them in the loop.
eng-sre: posting relevant logs, looks like sequence: model worker OOM -> nvidia driver reset (Xid 31) -> container crash loop.
eng-sre: snippet of /var/log/messages:```
Mar 12 03:14:21 infer-eu-n12 kernel: GPU 0000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 12 03:14:21 infer-eu-n12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (0000:03:00): 31, pid 2421, GPU:0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 12 03:14:22 containerd: container restart (code=137)
```
ops_oncall: running quick health checks. loading node-level telemetry now.
jen: telemetry shows memory pressure correlated with long sequences (>2048) from a small set of callers — likely unbounded prompt lengths causing KVCACHE pressure.
liam: can we route traffic off those hosts and scale down the seq-length for affected routes?
ops_oncall: taking nodes 12-15 out of rotation: `kubectl cordon infer-eu-n12 && kubectl drain infer-eu-n12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
samir: doing cordon/drain now. will keep 2 nodes spare for burst.
ops_oncall: also pushing immediate config change to routing: reduce max_seq_length to 1024 for route /v1/generate-eu to reduce KV pressure. deploy-bot: trigger deploy config change: deploy id 2024-rt-891
deploy-bot: rollout started for config/route-limit on namespace inference-eu (canary 5%).
maria: restarting NVIDIA driver on drained nodes after cordon: `sudo systemctl stop kubelet && sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm nvidia && sudo systemctl start kubelet` — doing this sequentially to avoid mass driver churn.
ops_oncall: note: rebooting infra could cause longer downtime for active customers, prefer driver reload + reimage if repeats.
eng-sre: adding temporary autoscale cap to avoid driving more pods onto other noisy hosts.
liam: what's ETA on nodes healthy?
samir: nodes 12/13 restarted drivers, KVCACHE freed, containers back up, no Xid seen for 5m. nodes 14/15 still draining.
cs-bridge: just notified alpha-game support: they see elevated 5xx but overall response resumed on canary routes.
eng-sre: root cause hypothesis: unbounded user prompts -> oversized KV cache growth + an older driver/kernel interaction causing sporadic Xid 31 under memory pressure. second-order contributor: a recent model rollout with longer average context lengths.
ops_oncall: mitigation actions summary: 1) cordon/drain noisy hosts; 2) restart driver's nvidia_uvm + modprobe sequence; 3) route config to cap seq length to 1024; 4) rollback recent model variant for EU canaries (if regressions).
jen: rolling back model-bert-extended-v3 canary for EU now. deploy-bot: rollback started (id 2024-mr-430).
eng-sre: monitoring for repeat Xid events. creating temporary alert to escalate if rate > 5/min for 10m.
samir: added flamegraph traces and kvcache usage per-pod to the dashboard.
ops_oncall: doc update for runbook note: prefer driver reload over immediate node reboot; when multiple nodes show Xid histogram spike, cordon and sequentially reboot/drain to avoid global capacity loss.
liam: do we want to proactively evacuate any other nodes with similar memory profile?
maria: running `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv` across nodes to find heavy consumers, will kill runaway pods if necessary.
eng-sre: killed 2 runaway debug pods on infer-eu-n9 consuming 40GB each. memory pressure dropped in cluster.
cs-bridge: customer comms: sent initial note that we saw driver resets, routing mitigations applied, will follow up with RCA.
ops_oncall: passing oncall to jen for 8h window for follow-up and RCA. jen: taking handoff.
jen: summary I'll capture in the incident tracker: timeline, nodes affected, mitigation commands, customer impact (alpha-game: brief 10-15m elevated errors; docsai-pro: minor retries), and next steps (postmortem, driver/kernel upgrade plan, stronger per-route seq caps).
eng-sre: tagging follow-ups: add kvcache eviction heuristics to Optimize, schedule test with upgraded NVIDIA driver (r535->r545) in staging, add automated detection for runaway context lengths.
samir: will prepare telemetry dump for postmortem (logs, kvcache histograms, pod-level memory).
jen: thanks all — closing this thread. we will reopen if Xid resumes or customers report new errors. :white_check_mark:
